research_rationale:
Executive Order 14059 (December 15, 2021, 86 FR 71549) declares a national emergency with respect to international drug trafficking and authorizes sanctions on foreign persons involved in the global illicit drug trade. The order is operative on 2026-10-14. Its text has no sunset, expiry condition or revocation trigger. The order itself declared the emergency, so it depends on the emergency staying in force under the National Emergencies Act; the held Presidential notices of December 12, 2022 (87 FR 76549), December 13, 2023 (88 FR 86809), December 11, 2024 (89 FR 100719) and December 10, 2025 (90 FR 57865) continue it year by year, and the last one continues it beyond December 15, 2025, to a date after the cutoff. The held eCFR text of 31 CFR 599.201 and 599.802, checked as of 2026-10-14, still implements the order, and an OFAC notice of October 6, 2026 (91 FR 63664) is held in the packet and shows continued operation of sanctions under it. Only section 1(c) and a reference in section 10 depend on the Fentanyl Sanctions Act; its text is not held in the packet. The eCFR authority citation for 31 CFR part 599, checked as of 2026-10-14, still lists 21 U.S.C. 2301 et seq., the U.S. Code note at 21 U.S.C. 2355 (current through 2026-10-09) refers to the Act as classified at 21 U.S.C. 2301 et seq., and no held source shows it repealed or expired; the remaining clauses rest on IEEPA and the National Emergencies Act. Executive Order 14097 of April 27, 2023 invokes 10 U.S.C. 12302 to respond to the national emergency declared in this order; it recites and relies on the order and does not revoke, amend or supersede it. The Federal Register disposition note lists only cross-references (Executive Order 14097 and the Notice of December 10, 2025).
